diff --git a/cache.py b/cache.py
index 1111111..2222222 100644
--- a/cache.py
+++ b/cache.py
@@ -10,8 +10,14 @@ class Cache:
     def get(self, key):
-        return self._store.get(key)
+        entry = self._store.get(key)
+        if entry is None:
+            return None
+        value, expires_at = entry
+        if expires_at < time.time():
+            del self._store[key]
+            return None
+        return value
 
-    def set(self, key, value):
-        self._store[key] = value
+    def set(self, key, value, ttl_seconds=60):
+        self._store[key] = (value, time.time() + ttl_seconds)
question: What does this change do, and what breaks if it's wrong?
answer: This adds expiry to the cache. Each entry now stores a value plus an expiry timestamp set from a TTL (default 60s) passed to set(). get() checks whether the stored expiry has passed; if so, it deletes the entry and returns None instead of the stale value. If this were implemented wrong -- say the expiry check compared the wrong timestamp, or set() didn't store expires_at at all -- get() would either return stale values forever (cache never expires) or expire everything immediately (cache never actually caches anything).
